$comment: Maximum findings each rule may report across the pinned corpus in scripts/corpus-scan.ts. This is a RATCHET: lower it whenever the scan reports a rule under budget. Raising an entry requires `npx tsx scripts/corpus-scan.ts --update` so the increase is reviewable and deliberate. A rule absent from this file is budgeted at 0, so a newly-noisy rule cannot arrive unnoticed.

triage.browser-security/no-eval: okta-signin-widget scripts/buildtools/commands/generate-phone-codes.js: axios.get(METADATA_URI).then(({data}) => { ... eval(data) }). Evaluating a payload fetched over the network — the strongest true positive in this batch. A build script, so it is their risk to accept, but the rule is exactly right.
triage.browser-security/no-unencrypted-transmis: ioredis lib/utils/index.ts: `new URL('redis://' + rawUrl)` — a dummy scheme prepended so URL() can parse a protocol-less host:port, per the target's own comment. Nothing is transmitted. The rule deliberately OWNS redis:// (no other rule covers the non-web cleartext protocols) and matches the scheme wherever it appears, including `new URLSearchParams`. Exempting URL parsers was considered and rejected: `const u = new URL('redis://host'); client.connect(u)` would then go silent, because the connect site carries no literal. Budgeted rather than narrowed — a recall loss is the worse trade for a security rule.
triage.node-security/no-toctou-vulnerability: okta-auth-js rollup.config.js: `if (!existsSync(d)) mkdirSync(d, {recursive:true})`. NOT a false positive. An exemption was written and reverted: with recursive:true an attacker who plants a symlink in the window gets mkdir to succeed SILENTLY and later writes follow it, where plain mkdir throws EEXIST and the program notices. The flag makes the race worse. Budgeted because the finding is correct and the target is a build script we do not control.
triage.node-security/require-dependency-integri: Shopify/cli, three HTML template literals that pull Polaris and graphiql CSS from jsdelivr and unpkg with no integrity= attribute. All three are correct SRI findings. Note error-page.ts: my own grep for external URLs MISSED it because the href is an interpolated constant (${POLARIS_STYLESHEET_URL}); the rule saw it and I did not.
triage.secure-coding/no-redos-vulnerable-regex:
7 -> 5 -> 7. REVERSED. The ratchet to 5 came from asking the oracle for the DEGREE rather than only whether the pattern is vulnerable at all, and then defaulting degree 2 off. Two of those findings are quadratic over short, sized input (^###\s+(.+)$ over one markdown heading) and nobody would act on them, so under Google's effective-FP standard the ratchet looked right.

The CWE-1333 recall gate rejected it. benchmarks/corpus/CWE-1333/vulnerable/trade-off.js pins /^(a*).*b/ as must-detect and recheck scores it degree 2, so the default dropped a detection. Degree only PROXIES the question that decides actionability — does the caller size the input — and nothing in the AST answers it. When the proxy and the calibrated corpus disagree, a security rule keeps the finding. Default flipped back to reporting; the quieter bar is opt-in via reportSecondDegreePolynomial: false and costs recall by construction.

So 2 of these 7 are known effective FPs, recorded rather than hidden. Buying them off with a default that costs a true positive was the wrong trade; the real fix is a bounded-input signal, which does not exist yet.

What DID survive: the rig now installs recheck. It never had, and recheck is an optional peer whose absence makes confirmsRedos fail open, so every ReDoS number recorded here before 2026-08-20 was measured with the oracle switched off. Installing it changed the count by zero — all 7 are oracle-confirmed.
triage.secure-coding/no-sensitive-data-exposure:
6 -> 2, ratcheted DOWN. Both survivors are REAL and neither should be silenced: Shopify bin/github-utils.js:37 `console.log(`Using token from ${source}: ${tokenFromEnv}`)` and :43 `console.log(`Using password from dev: ${password}`)` log an actual credential value.

The four that went away were one shape: the static PROSE names a credential while every interpolated VALUE names itself an outcome — twilio TokenAuthStrategy.ts:22, ApiTokenManager.ts:36, OrgsTokenManager.ts:36 (`Failed to fetch access token: ${error.message}`, `Error Status Code: ${error.status}`) and Shopify graphiql-token-provider.ts:38 (`Token request failed with status ${tokenResponse.status}`). The label describes the operation that FAILED; the property says what is actually printed. Property is structure, prose is not, so the property wins.

Two report paths had to be closed, not one. The text heuristic fired on label-separator-hole, and the VALUE path fired separately on `tokenResponse.status` by reading the RECEIVER's name and ignoring what was taken from it — the same defect VALUE_FREE_PROPERTIES already fixed for `.length`, one property set over. DIAGNOSTIC_ACCESSORS (message, stack, name, status, statusText) is protocol-grounded the same way: Error.prototype and the Fetch response, not vocabulary. `code` is deliberately excluded — an authorization code, a 2FA code and a recovery code are all called `code`.

Recall unchanged: CWE corpus 69/69, FP=0. Six FN guards pin the two real corpus leaks, an opaque hole under the same label, a mixed template, `code`, and a computed read.
triage.node-security/require-stream-error-handl:
4, and all 4 are TRUE POSITIVES. Re-examined 2026-08-21 because 'there is an error handler three lines up' made them look like obvious FPs. They are not, and the question is always WHICH STREAM the handler is attached to:

Shopify archiver.ts:55 and :163 blame `output`, the write stream. `archive.on('error')` covers the archiver; `output` has only an 'close' listener, so a disk-full or EACCES on the destination is an uncaught exception. .pipe() does not forward errors in either direction.

okta ImageDiff.js:12 blames `fs.createReadStream(image)`. The chained `.on('error', reject)` attaches to the PNG DESTINATION, not the source, so ENOENT on a missing image is unhandled — the classic pipe gotcha the rule exists for.

okta ImageDiff.js:63 has no handler on either end at all.

Do not 'fix' this rule by treating a nearby .on('error') as coverage. Any such change must keep these four reporting.
triage.node-security/no-unsafe-buffer-alloc:
3, all `new Array(length)` in redis/ioredis lib/resp/decoder.ts (669, 735, 803). Kept. `length` is the RESP wire length prefix, so it is decided by the server on the other end of the socket, and the rule's own measured note explains why this shape matters: the cost is a narrow band below V8's packed-elements limit (~33.5M), where 12 wire bytes buy 229 MB, rather than a monotonic function of n.

Weaker threat model than a public HTTP input — it takes a compromised or MITM'd Redis server — which is why these are budgeted rather than treated as must-fix. Not silenced: the rationale is measured and written down, and `new Array` is in SIZED_ALLOCATORS on purpose.
